summary: Milestone 2026.04.97 was orchestration-bound, not compute-bound. The conductor log shows about 172 minutes from activation at 2026-05-04T05:11Z to the final retro failure at 2026-05-04T08:03Z, but only two experiments reached status=complete: exp1248 Boltzmann-GPT CD training v2 and exp1251 NRGPT frozen-prefix evaluation v2. Most work ended as stale in_progress skeleton artifacts, repeated no-file-change attempts, or gate blocks. Both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout with no gpu_monitor.py-class zombie processes.
wall_time_basis: ops/conductor-log.md activation row at 2026-05-04 05:11 UTC through final exp1254 failure row at 2026-05-04 08:03 UTC; artifact mtime window was 2026-05-04T05:22:57Z through 2026-05-04T08:01:19Z.
experiments_blocked: exp1246: gate-blocked on retired/missing exp1244 and exp1245 outputs; no result artifact observed
exp1253: blocked_gate_check_failed because WOPR scope matched 12 prior artifacts and prior_failures was missing

slowest_experiments.title: Boltzmann-GPT CD Training v2
slowest_experiments.duration_basis: conductor-log window from previous lane completion at 06:24 UTC through OK at 06:42 UTC; one bootstrap failure plus successful post-test
slowest_experiments.why_long: This was the only substantial successful training/evaluation lane: 100 CD steps, FoVer sampling, AUROC measurement, then 81 focused tests. It also paid one failed artifact bootstrap attempt before completion.

slowest_experiments.title: Q11 TSS Instrumentation
slowest_experiments.duration_basis: conductor-log window from 07:26 UTC through third failed attempt at 07:43 UTC
slowest_experiments.why_long: Three serial attempts ended in artifact_not_updated_past_bootstrap or no file changes. The task was intended as a small diagnostic implementation, so the time was almost entirely retry/orchestration loss.

slowest_experiments.title: Figure Integrity Audit + fig3 Fix
slowest_experiments.duration_basis: conductor-log window from 05:53 UTC through third failed attempt at 06:09 UTC
slowest_experiments.why_long: The task repeatedly wrote or preserved only a skeleton/no-change state. Because exp1246 depended on exp1245, the failed audit also blocked the arXiv lane.

slowest_experiments.title: LLMs Gaming Verifiers Defense v3
slowest_experiments.duration_basis: conductor-log window from 06:42 UTC through third failed attempt at 06:58 UTC
slowest_experiments.why_long: The scope had been reduced to 10 samples, but the agent still stopped before terminal artifact reconciliation. The elapsed time came from repeated failed launches, not verifier compute.

slowest_experiments.title: Verifier Orthogonality Audit v2
slowest_experiments.duration_basis: conductor-log window from 05:39 UTC through third failed attempt at 05:53 UTC
slowest_experiments.why_long: This was a critical gate-producing task, but all attempts ended before computing the matrix. Its failure blocked exp1246 and kept the paper path idle.

bottlenecks_identified: The dominant bottleneck was stale skeleton churn: nine artifacts remained status=in_progress after conductor-level failure rows.
The conductor retried artifact_not_updated_past_bootstrap and no-file-change failures three times per task, even when the failure mode was deterministic.
The queue was effectively sequential despite many unconditional tasks in the v97 roadmap; CPU/doc/analysis work and GPU-eligible work were not overlapped.
GPU utilization was inefficient: exp1247, exp1248, and exp1250 were GPU-eligible, but the closeout monitor showed both RTX 3090s idle at 4 MB and 0% utilization.
No gpu_monitor.py-class zombie process was observed: the monitor reported no GPU processes and no warnings. The 4 MB allocations look like idle driver/context residue, not material VRAM waste.
Prior-failures governance still failed operationally: exp1253 DOOMED_RERUN_BLOCK repeated three times even after exp1230 had shipped an autofill script in the prior milestone.
The failure-ledger scope for WOPR cartridges remains too broad: a new Masyu cartridge was classified against 12 previous WOPR artifacts as a rerun without required priors.

Pre-flight was not the visible .97 bottleneck. The v97 plan used skip_pre_test for most experiments, and conductor failures were artifact bootstrap, no-file-change, gate-block, or DOOMED_RERUN_BLOCK rather than pre-test self-heal failures.
Doc reconciliation was inefficient in status semantics rather than wall-clock cost: ops/changelog.md accumulated duplicate in_progress lines while artifacts were not reconciled to terminal status.
Critical path coupling remained high: exp1244 and exp1245 blocked exp1246, so two failed gate producers made the arXiv lane idle immediately.
The milestone retro itself repeated the same bootstrap failure pattern it was supposed to evaluate, leaving exp1254 in_progress.
improvements_suggested: Run prior_failures autofill at milestone activation and fail the plan before dispatch if any task still lacks required priors.
Add a stale-skeleton finalizer: after an agent exits, the conductor must rewrite the artifact to terminal status complete, blocked, or failed with the exact failure reason.
Stop retrying no-file-change and artifact_not_updated_past_bootstrap three times by default; after the second identical failure, emit a terminal failed artifact and move on.
Use a parallel scheduler for v98: run exp-style CPU/doc/analysis tasks in at least two CPU lanes while one GPU lane handles GRPO, Boltzmann-GPT, or Phase-5-D.
Promote gpu_monitor.py from passive reporting to scheduling input: when both GPUs are idle and queued GPU-eligible tasks exist, dispatch or resume one immediately.
Record per-experiment GPU samples in result artifacts so retros can distinguish declared GPU eligibility from actual GPU residency/utilization.
Narrow failure-ledger scope keys for WOPR cartridges so a new puzzle cartridge is not treated as a rerun of every previous WOPR game unless files or deliverables overlap directly.
Make gate-blocks write structured result artifacts for the blocked task, including duration_s=0 and upstream fields, so operational accounting does not rely only on conductor logs.
Batch changelog/status/roadmap reconciliation once per terminal artifact and deduplicate repeated in_progress append lines.
For retro tasks, move criterion evaluation into a deterministic script or conductor helper instead of relying on long-form agent reasoning after STEP 0.
estimated_time_savings_rationale: A conservative 42% saving is plausible: roughly 20-25% from parallel dispatch of independent v97 tasks, 10-12% from stopping repeated stale-skeleton/no-file-change retries, 5-8% from activation-time prior-failures autofill and structured gate artifacts, and a smaller gain from batched reconciliation. That would reduce a 172 minute sequential retry-heavy milestone toward about 100 minutes even before research quality improves.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Implement conductor-side terminal artifact finalization for every launched task.
Run prior_failures autofill and WOPR scope validation before queue activation.
Adopt a default parallel schedule with one GPU lane plus at least two CPU/doc/analysis lanes.

gpu_utilization.assessment: Inefficient. Both GPUs were idle at closeout, and the conductor log does not show evidence that GPU-eligible exp1247, exp1248, or exp1250 occupied a live GPU lane. The milestone appears sequential and retry-bound rather than actively scheduled across devices.

zombie_process_assessment.basis: scripts/gpu_monitor.py reported no GPU processes and no warnings; supplied and rerun snapshots both showed only 4 MB allocated per GPU at 0% utilization.
zombie_process_assessment.note: There was no material zombie VRAM waste. The waste was idle capacity.

preflight_assessment: Not the main .97 bottleneck. Unlike .92-.94, the relevant conductor rows for .97 do not show pre-test self-heal failures. The blocking modes were stale skeletons, no file changes, gate blocks, and missing prior_failures.
doc_reconciliation_assessment: Inefficient but not because docs consumed most wall time. The issue was repeated in_progress changelog lines and missing terminal artifact reconciliation. Changelog/status/roadmap updates should be batched after terminal artifacts exist.
parallelization_assessment: exp1242, exp1243, exp1244, exp1245, exp1247, exp1248, exp1249, exp1250, exp1251, exp1252, and exp1253 were largely independent except for exp1246 depending on exp1244+exp1245 and exp1254 needing to run last. A three-lane scheduler could have overlapped most of the retry churn and kept GPU-eligible work separate from CPU/docs work.

question_answers.which_experiments_took_longest_and_why: The slowest observed lane was exp1248 at about 18 minutes because it had one bootstrap failure plus actual CD training/evaluation and focused tests. exp1252, exp1245, exp1249, and exp1244 followed at about 14-17 minutes, mostly due to three serial failed attempts rather than compute.
question_answers.was_gpu_utilization_efficient: No. Both RTX 3090s were idle at closeout, and the milestone ran as a mostly sequential retry queue. GPU-eligible tasks could have occupied a GPU lane while CPU/doc tasks ran separately.
question_answers.were_there_zombie_processes: No formal zombies were detected. gpu_monitor.py saw no GPU processes and no warnings; the 4 MB allocations per GPU were negligible.
question_answers.could_experiments_have_been_parallelized: Yes. Most v97 tasks were unconditional. Only exp1246 was gated on exp1244 and exp1245, and exp1254 was intended as the final retro. The rest could have run across CPU/doc and GPU lanes.
question_answers.was_preflight_a_bottleneck: No for .97. The pre-flight suite was not the visible blocker in the conductor log; stale skeletons and gate/prior-failure checks were.
question_answers.were_doc_reconciliation_passes_efficient: No. They did not dominate wall time, but reconciliation semantics were poor: duplicate in_progress changelog entries accumulated and artifacts remained non-terminal.
question_answers.what_tooling_would_speed_next_milestone: Terminal artifact finalization, activation-time prior_failures autofill, narrower WOPR rerun scope keys, active gpu_monitor-driven scheduling, per-experiment GPU utilization sampling, structured gate-block artifacts, and a default parallel scheduler.

meta_reflection: The STEP 0 skeleton pattern is now doing its original job: it prevents total artifact loss. But .97 shows the second-order failure clearly. Skeletons have become a stable failure state because the conductor does not enforce terminal reconciliation after agent exit. The next operational win is not asking agents to remember better; it is making the conductor finalize, block, or fail artifacts deterministically and scheduling independent work in parallel while that happens.
